Features

# What Kyro does

A private crypto wallet: send, receive, swap and stake on 36 blockchains from one recovery phrase, over Tor, and read every transaction before it is signed.

Portfolio

## All your coins in one list

Total value, a price chart from one day to all time, and every asset with its balance, 7-day trend and share.

- Market tab with the top 200 coins, and favourites.

- Search assets and addresses with Ctrl K.

- Allocation by asset, and a vault panel with your security status.

================================================================
Security: how Kyro Wallet protects your keys
URL: https://kyrowallet.com/security/
================================================================

Security

# How Kyro protects your keys

Encrypted on your computer, confirmed in a system window. Here is what that covers, and what it does not.

Design

## Three layers, one place for keys

The interface you click is a sandboxed web view. It never sees a key. Keys live only in the Rust core, which encrypts them, signs and returns the signed transaction.

- Recovery phrase and keys encrypted with your password: Argon2id, then XChaCha20-Poly1305.

- Stored only on your computer. No copy on a server, no cloud backup.

- Standard 12 or 24-word BIP39 recovery phrases.

01

InterfaceSandboxed web view. Never sees a key.

02

App shellTor, auto-lock, system confirmation window.

03

Rust coreEncryption, keys and signing.

Before you sign

## Nothing is signed without you

Every signature needs your password and a confirmation in a native system window, drawn by the app shell, outside the web view.

- The window shows the decoded transaction: amount, recipient, fee, account.

- Unusual transactions ask for a second confirmation: contract calls, any token approval, value sent to a contract, an unknown chain ID, high fees.

- Token approvals are for the exact amount by default.

- Address-poisoning alerts and clipboard checks before you send.

Network

## Private by default

Kyro talks to blockchains over Tor, which is built into the app. Your IP address is not linked to your addresses.

- A separate Tor circuit per blockchain.

- If Tor fails, Kyro stops. It never falls back to a direct connection.

- Every server Kyro contacts is listed in NETWORK.md.

- Use your own node or server for each blockchain.

- No personal data, no analytics, no account. Only an anonymous weekly count over Tor, which you can turn off.

Limits

## What Kyro cannot protect you from

No wallet can. Knowing these helps you avoid them.

- Malware with full control of your computer while the wallet is unlocked.

- Anyone who gets your recovery phrase. Kyro never asks for it outside the app, and neither should anyone else.

- A transaction you read and confirm. Check the recipient and amount in the system window every time.

- A lost recovery phrase. Kyro has no copy and cannot reset it. Write it on paper and keep it offline.

## Audit status

Kyro is open source under GPL-3.0-or-later, so anyone can review it. An internal security review has been done. No external audit has been published yet. Kyro is provided without warranty, as stated in the license.

Threat model Servers contacted Architecture

## Report a vulnerability

Please report security issues privately through GitHub security advisories, not in a public issue. The security policy explains what is in scope and how reports are handled.

Scams

## Built against the usual tricks

Most losses start with a trick, so Kyro checks for the common ones before you sign.

### Address poisoning

A blocking alert when a recipient looks like a known address without being it. The server's history is never trusted. How it works

### Clipboard swaps

After you paste, Kyro watches the field, and shows the address in blocks. A swap before the paste can only be caught by comparing with your source.

### Unlimited approvals

Approvals are exact by default. An unlimited one needs an explicit action and shows a warning.

### Booby-trapped text

Memos and token names from the chain are cleaned of line breaks, bidi and invisible characters before you read them.

### Booby-trapped updates

Each update is signed, and verified against a public key pinned in the app.

### Unknown servers

A new custom server is confirmed in a system window before any request goes out.

## Keep reading

### Back up your recovery phrase

The one thing Kyro cannot do for you.

### How Kyro uses Tor

Who sees what, and what happens when Tor is down.

### Read, build and verify

Check the claims on this page yourself.

Fees

# Kyro is free. Swaps from 0.7%.

Sending, receiving and staking cost only the network fee. Swaps carry a Kyro fee based on the swap value, already out of the amount you receive.

Swap value$200

Kyro fee1.11%

Fee in dollars$2.22

You receive, in value$197.78

0% Send and receive You pay the network fee only.

0% Staking SOL, ADA, TRX, NEAR. Network fee only.

from 0.7% Swaps Included in the amount you receive.

## Swap fee by swap value

The Kyro fee is a percentage of the swap. Small swaps pay a higher rate and large swaps a lower one. The value is the size of the swap in US dollars.

Kyro swap fee by swap value in US dollars

| Swap value (USD) | Kyro fee

| $5 or less | 5%

| $10 | 2%

| $25 | 1.8%

| $50 | 1.6%

| $80 | 1.4%

| $100 | 1.2%

| $1,000 | 0.9%

| $10,000 and above | 0.7%

How it is calculated:  The table gives the rate at each listed value. Between two values the rate moves smoothly, interpolated on a logarithmic scale, so there are no sudden jumps.

Unknown token price:  If Kyro cannot find a price for the token, it cannot work out the swap value. The fee is then 0.9%.

Already included:  The fee is deducted from the amount you receive. Kyro shows only what you send and what you receive, so the "you receive" amount is what arrives, with no further Kyro charge.

Example

## A $200 swap

$200 falls between the $100 and $1,000 rows, so the rate is between 1.2% and 0.9%: about 1.11%.

You send200 USDC ~ $200

Kyro fee, about 1.11%~ $2.22 already deducted

You receive~ $197.78 in the token you chose

Network feeSeparate, paid to the network

## How the swap fee works

- The rate depends on the swap value, from 0.7% to 5%. It is already part of the quote: the amount you receive is after the fee.

- It is collected by each provider's official integrator fee option. Exolix has none: on Exolix routes (Monero, Kaspa, Algorand and NEAR) the fee is a second transfer on the source chain.

- Quotes are compared after fees: the best price shown already includes them.

- If a provider cannot apply the fee correctly, its quote is not shown.

- Providers may charge their own fee. It is already in the price they quote.

## Network fees

Every blockchain charges a fee to process a transaction. It goes to the network's miners or validators, not to Kyro. Kyro estimates it and shows it before you confirm. On Ethereum layer 2s like Arbitrum, Optimism and Base it is usually a few cents; on Bitcoin and Ethereum it changes with demand.

## Why a swap fee

The fee pays for development. Kyro is open source, so the fee is public: the schedule is set in the code, and anyone can build a version without it. Full details are in SWAP_FEES.md.

Kyro fees by action

| Action | Kyro fee | Network fee

| Receive | 0% | None

| Send | 0% | Yes

| Stake, unstake | 0% | Yes

| Swap | From 0.7% | Yes

Exolix routes

## One route, two transfers

Monero, Kaspa, Algorand and NEAR go through Exolix, which has no integrator fee.

### Same rate

The curve is the same as on every other route, taken from the amount you sell.

### Second transfer

The Kyro fee is a second ordinary transfer of the sold coin to Kyro's fee address on that chain. You approve it, and it carries its own network fee.

### No separate transfer elsewhere

On other routes the fee is collected through the provider's official integrator mechanism.

## Keep reading

### Swap routes and limits

Which coin goes where, and through whom.

### Swap to Monero

A worked example, step by step.

# Download Kyro Wallet

Free for Windows, macOS and Linux. One command, or the file yourself. Kyro is published only on GitHub Releases.

Download Kyro Release notes

8:  active wallets this week93:  downloads in total

Recommended

## Install with one command

Paste the command for your system into PowerShell (Windows) or Terminal (macOS, Linux). It downloads the latest release from GitHub, checks its SHA-256 and installs it. A file fetched this way is not marked as downloaded from the internet, so Windows SmartScreen and macOS Gatekeeper do not block the first launch.

Windows · PowerShell

irm https://kyrowallet.com/install.ps1 | iex

macOS and Linux · Terminal

curl -fsSL https://kyrowallet.com/install.sh | sh

Downloads the latest release from GitHub, checks its SHA-256 against SHA256SUMS, then installs it. The scripts are open source: install.ps1 · install.sh (website/src).

On Windows the usual installer window opens. On macOS Kyro goes to Applications; on Linux to ~/.local/bin/kyro with a menu entry. No administrator password is asked by the script.

Or

## Download the file

Windows .exe installer    macOS Apple Silicon & Intel    Linux AppImage

Q: Downloaded the file in your browser?
A: The installers are not code-signed yet, so Windows and macOS show a warning the first time you open a file downloaded by a browser. Verify the checksum first, then:

### Windows: "Windows protected your PC"

- Click More info.

- Check that the file name is Kyro-windows-x64-setup.exe.

- Click Run anyway.

### macOS: "Kyro can't be opened"

- Drag Kyro into Applications.

- Right-click Kyro in Applications and choose Open, then Open again.

- Or go to System Settings > Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway.

### Linux

```
chmod +x Kyro-linux-x86_64.AppImage
./Kyro-linux-x86_64.AppImage
# or
sudo apt install ./Kyro-linux-amd64.deb
```

The AppImage needs FUSE 2: sudo apt install libfuse2t64 (Ubuntu 24.04 and later) or libfuse2 (older releases).

For a hardware wallet over USB on Linux, install the Ledger or Trezor udev rules.

## All files

Kyro 1.0.6 release files

| File | System | Notes

| Kyro-windows-x64-setup.exe | Windows 64-bit | Installer, recommended

| Kyro-windows-x64.msi | Windows 64-bit | MSI package, for managed installs

| Kyro-macos.dmg | macOS | Apple Silicon and Intel

| Kyro-linux-x86_64.AppImage | Linux x86_64 | Runs on most distributions

| Kyro-linux-amd64.deb | Debian, Ubuntu | Package for apt

| SHA256SUMS | All | SHA-256 checksums of every file

Only from GitHub. The files above come from github.com/shuntraa/kyro-wallet/releases. A copy offered anywhere else is not from us. Kyro has no mobile app: anything in an app store using the name is not ours.

Checksum

## Verify your download

The install commands do this for you. If you downloaded a file yourself, download SHA256SUMS next to it, compute the SHA-256 of your file and compare it with the matching line. If they differ, delete the file and download it again.

### Windows (PowerShell)

```
Get-FileHash .\Kyro-windows-x64-setup.exe -Algorithm SHA256
```

### macOS (Terminal)

```
shasum -a 256 Kyro-macos.dmg
```

### Linux

```
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing
```

Source

## Build it yourself

You need Rust, Node.js 22+, pnpm 11 and the Tauri prerequisites. See the README.

```
git clone https://github.com/shuntraa/kyro-wallet.git
cd kyro-wallet
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm build
```

20 questions

# Frequently asked questions

Can't find yours? Ask on GitHub.

## The basics

Q: Is Kyro Wallet free?
A: Yes. Kyro is free to download and use, and open source under GPL-3.0-or-later. Sending, receiving and staking cost only the network fee. Swaps from 0.7%, built into the rate. Fee details.

Q: Is Kyro custodial?
A: No. Kyro is non-custodial. Your keys are created and encrypted on your computer. There is no account and no server holding your funds, so nobody, including us, can freeze, move or recover them.

Q: Which blockchains does Kyro support?
A: 36 blockchains: Bitcoin, Ethereum, BNB Chain, Polygon, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Avalanche, Cronos, Mantle, Sonic, Flare, Kaia, Gnosis, HyperEVM, Sei, Conflux, Solana, TRON, Cardano, XRP Ledger, Litecoin, Dogecoin, Bitcoin Cash, Dash, Stellar, NEAR, Sui, Monero, TON, Cosmos Hub, Polkadot, Aptos, Algorand, Kaspa and Zcash. Plus 220+ tokens on them. What works on each one.

Q: Which computers does Kyro run on?
A: Windows (64-bit), macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel) and Linux (x86_64 AppImage or .deb). Download.

Q: Is there a mobile app?
A: No. Kyro is a desktop app only. An app in a mobile store using the Kyro name is not ours.

## Swaps and staking

Q: Can I swap Monero in Kyro?
A: Yes, both ways, through Exolix. Kyro's fee is a second ordinary transfer of the coin you sell. Swap to Monero.

Q: Can I earn from a hardware wallet?
A: Lido and Aave work from Ledger and Trezor accounts. Staking on Solana, Cardano, TRON and NEAR needs a recovery-phrase account. Options and risks.

Q: How much does a swap cost?
A: The Kyro fee depends on the value of the swap: 5% for $5 or less, down to 0.7% from $10,000, and 0.9% if the token price is unknown. It is already taken out of the amount you receive. The blockchain charges a separate network fee, which goes to the network. Providers may add their own fee, already included in their quote. Full fee table.

Q: Can I stake with Kyro?
A: Yes. Earn lists 14 options: staking on Solana, Cardano, TRON and NEAR, ETH liquid staking with Lido, and lending on Aave. Rates are estimates, never guaranteed. Kyro takes no fee on staking, and nothing here is financial advice. Options and risks.

## Security

Q: Does Kyro support hardware wallets?
A: Yes: Ledger and Trezor, including Trezor Safe 7. Supported on Bitcoin, Ethereum, BNB Chain, Polygon, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Avalanche, Cronos, Mantle, Sonic, Flare, Kaia, Gnosis, HyperEVM, Sei, Conflux, Solana, TRON, Cardano, XRP Ledger, Litecoin, Dogecoin, Bitcoin Cash, Dash, Stellar, NEAR, Sui, TON, Cosmos Hub, Aptos, Algorand and Zcash.

Q: What happens if I lose my recovery phrase?
A: If you also lose your computer or password, your funds cannot be recovered. Kyro keeps no copy and cannot reset it. Write the phrase on paper, keep it offline, and never type it into a website.

Q: Can I import a recovery phrase from another wallet?
A: Yes. Kyro accepts standard 12 and 24-word BIP39 recovery phrases.

Q: Does Kyro use Tor?
A: Yes. Tor is built in and on by default, with a separate circuit per blockchain. If Tor fails, Kyro stops instead of connecting directly. You can also use your own servers.

Q: Does Kyro collect any data?
A: No personal data. No account, no analytics, no identifiers. Once a week, Kyro anonymously downloads a tiny file from its GitHub release over Tor, so GitHub's download counter can estimate how many wallets are active; you can turn it off in Settings, Privacy. Every server the app contacts is listed in NETWORK.md. This website sets no cookies; it only reads the public usage counters from GitHub.

Q: Is Kyro open source? Has it been audited?
A: The full source is on GitHub under GPL-3.0-or-later. An internal security review has been done. No external audit has been published yet.

Q: How do I report a vulnerability?
A: Privately, through GitHub security advisories. Please do not open a public issue. See the security policy.

## Download and install

Q: Where should I download Kyro?
A: Only from GitHub Releases, or from the links on kyrowallet.com/download, which point there.

Q: How do I verify my download?
A: Compare the SHA-256 of your file with the matching line in SHA256SUMS.

```
Get-FileHash .\Kyro-windows-x64-setup.exe -Algorithm SHA256   # Windows
shasum -a 256 Kyro-macos.dmg                                  # macOS
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing                      # Linux
```

Q: Windows says "Windows protected your PC". What do I do?
A: That is SmartScreen: the installer is not code-signed yet. Verify the checksum, then click More info and Run anyway. The one-line install command checks the checksum for you and does not trigger this warning.

Q: macOS says Kyro can't be opened. What do I do?
A: Right-click Kyro in Applications and choose Open, or go to System Settings > Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway.

Privacy policy | Kyro Wallet
URL: https://kyrowallet.com/privacy/
================================================================

Privacy

# Privacy policy

Kyro Wallet collects no personal data. There is no account and no analytics. Once a week, an anonymous download over Tor helps estimate how many wallets are active.

## What Kyro collects

No personal data. The Kyro developers do not receive any personal data from the app: no crash reports, no identifiers, no addresses, no balances. Kyro has no user accounts and no sign-up.

## Anonymous weekly count

Once a week, after you unlock Kyro and only over Tor, the app downloads a tiny file (ping.txt) from Kyro's latest GitHub release. Nothing is sent with it: no identifier, no version, no address. GitHub's public download counter for that file then gives an estimate of how many wallets are active each week; the only thing Kyro stores is the week it last did this. If Tor is off, it never happens. You can turn it off in Settings, Privacy, "Anonymous weekly count".

## Data on your device

Your recovery phrase and keys are encrypted with your password (Argon2id, then XChaCha20-Poly1305) and stored only on your computer. Settings, contacts and cached balances also stay on your computer. Nothing is backed up to a server or a cloud. Uninstalling Kyro and deleting its app folder removes this data; keep your recovery phrase on paper to restore your wallet.

## Network requests

To show balances, prices and history, and to send transactions and swaps, Kyro contacts only the blockchain, price and swap providers listed in NETWORK.md, which also says what each one sees. These requests go through the Tor network built into Kyro by default, so the providers do not see your IP address. They do see what you ask for: the public addresses you look up, the transactions you broadcast and, for swaps, the tokens, amounts and receiving address. Their own privacy policies apply to that data. You can use your own nodes and servers instead (Settings, Networks).

The website kyrowallet.com sets no cookies, uses no trackers or analytics and makes no third-party request. Everything it loads comes from the site itself, and its usage counters are written into the pages when the site is built.

## Contact

Questions about privacy: open an issue on GitHub. Security issues: report them privately through GitHub security advisories.

Last updated: 4 November 2026.

================================================================
Code signing policy | Kyro Wallet
URL: https://kyrowallet.com/code-signing-policy/
================================================================

Code signing

# Code signing policy

Free code signing provided by SignPath.io, certificate by SignPath Foundation.

## Status

Code signing through the SignPath Foundation program for open-source projects is planned and pending approval. Until it is approved, Kyro releases are not code signed (Windows SmartScreen shows a warning; see First launch). Automatic updates are signed separately with Kyro's update key and checked by the app. This page applies as soon as signing is active.

## What is signed

Only release builds of Kyro Wallet built by the public GitHub Actions release workflow of github.com/shuntraa/kyro-wallet, from a version tag, from the source code in that repository. Nothing built on a personal computer is signed, and the certificate is never used to sign anything else: no third-party software, no other project, no modified builds.

## Team roles

- Committers and reviewers: shuntraa (maintainer).

- Approvers (each signing request is approved by hand): shuntraa.

Every change to the repository goes through the maintainer.

## Privacy

Kyro collects no personal data and transfers no information to other networked systems unless you ask for it: the blockchain, price and swap requests you trigger go to the providers listed in NETWORK.md, over Tor by default. See the privacy policy.

## Report a problem

If you find a signed file that does not come from this project's release workflow, report it through GitHub security advisories.

Bitcoin desktop wallet · BTC

# Bitcoin wallet for Windows, macOS and Linux

Send, receive and swap BTC, and sign with a Ledger or Trezor. Kyro is free, open source and non-custodial: your keys stay on your own computer and traffic goes over Tor by default.

Download Kyro All blockchains

### Send and receive

Send and receive BTC, with address-poisoning alerts and clipboard checks.
Yes

### Swap

Swap BTC in the app. The amount you receive already includes Kyro's swap fee, from 0.7%.
Yes

### Earn

Kyro offers no staking or lending on Bitcoin.
No

### Hardware wallet

Sign Bitcoin transactions with a Ledger or Trezor.
Yes

Details

## Bitcoin in Kyro

- Native SegWit (bc1q...) and Taproot (bc1p...) addresses.

- Transactions are checked before you sign: unknown scripts, OP_RETURN data or a fee above 100 sat/vB ask for a second confirmation.

- Bitcoin has no native staking.

- Same recovery phrase as your other 35 blockchains.

- Keys encrypted on your computer; every signature confirmed in a system window.

All wallet features How swap fees work How your keys are protected

Questions

## Bitcoin questions

Q: Is Kyro a free Bitcoin wallet?
A: Yes. Kyro is free, open source and non-custodial. You pay the network fee when you send BTC, and your keys stay on your own computer.

Q: Can I swap BTC in Kyro?
A: Yes, in both directions. Providers: 1Click, LI.FI. Exolix to XMR, KAS, ALGO and NEAR. Routes and limits.

Q: Can I earn on Bitcoin in Kyro?
A: Kyro offers no staking or lending on Bitcoin.

Q: Does Kyro work with a hardware wallet on Bitcoin?
A: Yes, with a Ledger or Trezor. Device table.

Q: What can a server see when I use Bitcoin in Kyro?
A: The server sees the addresses and transactions you ask about, and the IP of a Tor exit relay, not yours. Bitcoin has its own circuit family, except that all EVM networks share one. Who sees what.

Q: Can I use my existing recovery phrase for Bitcoin?
A: Yes, if it is a standard 12 or 24-word BIP39 phrase. It covers all 36 blockchains. More questions.

Ethereum desktop wallet · ETH

# Ethereum wallet for Windows, macOS and Linux

Send, receive and swap ETH and ERC-20 tokens, and sign with a Ledger or Trezor. Kyro is free, open source and non-custodial: your keys stay on your own computer and traffic goes over Tor by default.

Download Kyro All blockchains

### Send and receive

Send and receive ETH and ERC-20 tokens, with address-poisoning alerts and clipboard checks.
Yes

### Swap

Swap ETH in the app. The amount you receive already includes Kyro's swap fee, from 0.7%.
Yes

### Earn

ETH liquid staking with Lido, and lending USDT, USDC, DAI and WETH on Aave. Rates are estimates.
Yes

### Hardware wallet

Sign Ethereum transactions with a Ledger or Trezor.
Yes

Details

## Ethereum in Kyro

- ETH and ERC-20 tokens in the same account.

- Token approvals are set to the exact amount by default. Unlimited approvals are off unless you turn them on.

- Contract calls, approvals and high fees ask for a second confirmation.

- Native ETH staking is not offered: it needs 32 ETH and a validator running at all times. Liquid staking with Lido and lending on Aave are in Earn.

- Same recovery phrase as your other 35 blockchains.

- Keys encrypted on your computer; every signature confirmed in a system window.

All wallet features How swap fees work How your keys are protected

At a glance

## Ethereum in one table

What works today, and through what.

What Kyro supports on Ethereum

|  | Available | Details

| Send and receive |  | ETH and ERC-20 tokens. Over Tor, with address-poisoning alerts.

| Swap from |  | Providers: 0x and LI.FI on the same chain. 1Click and LI.FI across chains. Exolix to XMR, KAS, ALGO and NEAR.

| Swap to |  | The amount you see already has Kyro's fee out.

| Earn |  | ETH liquid staking with Lido, and lending USDT, USDC, DAI and WETH on Aave.

| Ledger |  | Keys stay in the device.

| Trezor |  | Keys stay in the device.

Swap routes and limits Earn options and risks Ledger and Trezor in Kyro How Kyro uses Tor

Questions

## Ethereum questions

Q: Is Kyro a free Ethereum wallet?
A: Yes. Kyro is free, open source and non-custodial. You pay the network fee when you send ETH, and your keys stay on your own computer.

Q: Can I swap ETH in Kyro?
A: Yes, in both directions. Providers: 0x and LI.FI on the same chain. 1Click and LI.FI across chains. Exolix to XMR, KAS, ALGO and NEAR. Routes and limits.

Q: Can I earn on Ethereum in Kyro?
A: Yes: ETH liquid staking with Lido, and lending USDT, USDC, DAI and WETH on Aave. Rates are estimates, never guaranteed, and contract risks apply. Options and risks.

Q: Does Kyro work with a hardware wallet on Ethereum?
A: Yes, with a Ledger or Trezor. Device table.

Q: What can a server see when I use Ethereum in Kyro?
A: The server sees the addresses and transactions you ask about, and the IP of a Tor exit relay, not yours. Ethereum has its own circuit family, except that all EVM networks share one. Who sees what.

Q: Can I use my existing recovery phrase for Ethereum?
A: Yes, if it is a standard 12 or 24-word BIP39 phrase. It covers all 36 blockchains. More questions.

A: Yes. Kyro is free, open source and non-custodial. You pay the network fee when you send MNT, and your keys stay on your own computer.

Q: Can I swap MNT in Kyro?
A: Yes, in both directions. Providers: 0x or LI.FI, same chain only. Routes and limits.

Q: Can I earn on Mantle in Kyro?
A: Kyro offers no staking or lending on Mantle.

Q: Does Kyro work with a hardware wallet on Mantle?
A: Yes, with a Ledger or Trezor. Device table.

Q: What can a server see when I use Mantle in Kyro?
A: The server sees the addresses and transactions you ask about, and the IP of a Tor exit relay, not yours. Mantle has its own circuit family, except that all EVM networks share one. Who sees what.

Q: Can I use my existing recovery phrase for Mantle?
A: Yes, if it is a standard 12 or 24-word BIP39 phrase. It covers all 36 blockchains. More questions.

Solana desktop wallet · SOL

# Solana wallet for Windows, macOS and Linux

Send, receive, swap and stake SOL and SPL tokens, and sign with a Ledger or Trezor. Kyro is free, open source and non-custodial: your keys stay on your own computer and traffic goes over Tor by default.

Download Kyro All blockchains

### Send and receive

Send and receive SOL and SPL tokens, with address-poisoning alerts and clipboard checks.
Yes

### Swap

Swap SOL in the app. The amount you receive already includes Kyro's swap fee, from 0.7%.
Yes

### Earn

Stake SOL from your own account. Kyro takes no fee on staking. Rates are estimates.
Yes

### Hardware wallet

Sign Solana transactions with a Ledger or Trezor.
Yes

Details

## Solana in Kyro

Delegate SOL to a validator from a stake account in your name. Activation and cooldown take about one epoch each (around two days). A validator cannot take your SOL; your rewards depend on its commission and uptime.

- SOL, SPL and Token-2022 tokens.

- Versioned (v0) transactions and address lookup tables are decoded before you sign.

- Same recovery phrase as your other 35 blockchains.

- Keys encrypted on your computer; every signature confirmed in a system window.

All wallet features How swap fees work How your keys are protected

At a glance

## Solana in one table

What works today, and through what.

What Kyro supports on Solana

|  | Available | Details

| Send and receive |  | SOL and SPL tokens. Over Tor, with address-poisoning alerts.

| Swap from |  | Providers: Jupiter on Solana. LI.FI and 1Click across chains. Exolix for SOL, USDT and USDC.

| Swap to |  | The amount you see already has Kyro's fee out.

| Earn |  | Staking from your own account, with a recovery-phrase account only. Rates are estimates.

| Ledger |  | Keys stay in the device.

| Trezor |  | Keys stay in the device.

Swap routes and limits Earn options and risks Ledger and Trezor in Kyro How Kyro uses Tor

Questions

## Solana questions

Q: Is Kyro a free Solana wallet?
A: Yes. Kyro is free, open source and non-custodial. You pay the network fee when you send SOL, and your keys stay on your own computer.

Q: Can I swap SOL in Kyro?
A: Yes, in both directions. Providers: Jupiter on Solana. LI.FI and 1Click across chains. Exolix for SOL, USDT and USDC. Routes and limits.

Q: Can I stake SOL in Kyro?
A: Yes, from a recovery-phrase account. It is refused from a hardware wallet. Delegate SOL to a validator from a stake account in your name. Activation and cooldown take about one epoch each (around two days). A validator cannot take your SOL; your rewards depend on its commission and uptime. Rates are estimates, never guaranteed.

Q: Does Kyro work with a hardware wallet on Solana?
A: Yes, with a Ledger or Trezor. Device table.

Q: What can a server see when I use Solana in Kyro?
A: The server sees the addresses and transactions you ask about, and the IP of a Tor exit relay, not yours. Solana has its own circuit family, except that all EVM networks share one. Who sees what.

Q: Can I use my existing recovery phrase for Solana?
A: Yes, if it is a standard 12 or 24-word BIP39 phrase. It covers all 36 blockchains. More questions.

## TRON in Kyro

Stake TRX (Stake 2.0) for energy or bandwidth, then vote for Super Representatives with your TRON Power. Unstaking takes 14 days. Votes do not put your TRX at risk.

- TRX and TRC-20 tokens such as USDT.

- Energy and bandwidth from staking lower the cost of TRC-20 transfers.

- Same recovery phrase as your other 35 blockchains.

- Keys encrypted on your computer; every signature confirmed in a system window.

## TRON in one table

What works today, and through what.

What Kyro supports on TRON

|  | Available | Details

| Send and receive |  | TRX and TRC-20 tokens. Over Tor, with address-poisoning alerts.

| Swap from |  | Providers: 1Click. Exolix.

| Swap to |  | The amount you see already has Kyro's fee out.

| Earn |  | Staking from your own account, with a recovery-phrase account only. Rates are estimates.

| Ledger |  | Keys stay in the device.

| Trezor |  | Not supported.

Swap routes and limits Earn options and risks Ledger and Trezor in Kyro How Kyro uses Tor

Questions

## TRON questions

Q: Is Kyro a free TRON wallet?
A: Yes. Kyro is free, open source and non-custodial. You pay the network fee when you send TRX, and your keys stay on your own computer.

Q: Can I swap TRX in Kyro?
A: Yes, in both directions. Providers: 1Click. Exolix. Routes and limits.

Q: Can I stake TRX in Kyro?
A: Yes, from a recovery-phrase account. It is refused from a hardware wallet. Stake TRX (Stake 2.0) for energy or bandwidth, then vote for Super Representatives with your TRON Power. Unstaking takes 14 days. Votes do not put your TRX at risk. Rates are estimates, never guaranteed.

Q: Does Kyro work with a hardware wallet on TRON?
A: Yes, with a Ledger. Device table.

Q: What can a server see when I use TRON in Kyro?
A: The server sees the addresses and transactions you ask about, and the IP of a Tor exit relay, not yours. TRON has its own circuit family, except that all EVM networks share one. Who sees what.

Q: Can I use my existing recovery phrase for TRON?
A: Yes, if it is a standard 12 or 24-word BIP39 phrase. It covers all 36 blockchains. More questions.

NEAR desktop wallet · NEAR

# NEAR wallet for Windows, macOS and Linux

Send, receive, swap and stake NEAR and USDC and USDT tokens, and sign with a Ledger. Kyro is free, open source and non-custodial: your keys stay on your own computer and traffic goes over Tor by default.

Download Kyro All blockchains

### Send and receive

Send and receive NEAR and USDC and USDT tokens, with address-poisoning alerts and clipboard checks.
Yes

### Swap

Swap native NEAR in and out through Exolix, without an account. Kyro's fee is a second ordinary transfer on NEAR. NEAR tokens are not offered. The amount you receive already includes Kyro's swap fee, from 0.7%.
Yes

### Earn

Stake NEAR from your own account. Kyro takes no fee on staking. Rates are estimates.
Yes

### Hardware wallet

Sign NEAR transactions with a Ledger. The Ledger account is a different account than the software wallet.
Yes

Details

## NEAR in Kyro

Stake with a NEAR staking pool from the official factories. Kyro checks the pool's code before each transaction. Unstaked NEAR stays locked for 4 epochs before you can withdraw it. With a Ledger account, staking is not available.

- NEAR Protocol mainnet.

- USDC and USDT on NEAR are supported.

- Same recovery phrase as your other 35 blockchains.

- Keys encrypted on your computer; every signature confirmed in a system window.

All wallet features How swap fees work How your keys are protected

Unstaked NEAR stays locked for 4 epochs before you can withdraw it. With a Ledger account, staking is not available. Rates are estimates, never guaranteed.

Questions

## Sui questions

Q: Is Kyro a free Sui wallet?
A: Yes. Kyro is free, open source and non-custodial. You pay the network fee when you send SUI, and your keys stay on your own computer.

Q: Can I swap SUI in Kyro?
A: Yes, in both directions. Providers: 1Click. Routes and limits.

Q: Can I earn on Sui in Kyro?

Q: Does Kyro work with a hardware wallet on Sui?
A: Yes, with a Ledger. Device table.

Q: What can a server see when I use Sui in Kyro?
A: The server sees the addresses and transactions you ask about, and the IP of a Tor exit relay, not yours. Sui has its own circuit family, except that all EVM networks share one. Who sees what.

Q: Can I use my existing recovery phrase for Sui?
A: Yes, if it is a standard 12 or 24-word BIP39 phrase. It covers all 36 blockchains. More questions.

Monero wallet for Windows, macOS and Linux | Kyro
URL: https://kyrowallet.com/chains/monero/
================================================================

Monero desktop wallet · XMR

# Monero wallet for Windows, macOS and Linux

Send, receive and swap XMR. Kyro is free, open source and non-custodial: your keys stay on your own computer and traffic goes over Tor by default.

Download Kyro All blockchains

### Send and receive

Send and receive XMR, with address-poisoning alerts and clipboard checks.
Yes

### Swap

Swap XMR both ways through Exolix, without an account. Kyro's fee is a second ordinary transfer of the coin you sell. The amount you receive already includes Kyro's swap fee, from 0.7%.
Yes

### Earn

Kyro offers no staking or lending on Monero.
No

### Hardware wallet

Not supported on Monero yet. Use a software account.
No

Details

## Monero in Kyro

- Your Kyro recovery phrase restores your Monero wallet too. To move it to another Monero wallet, Kyro can also show the matching 25-word Monero phrase, which works in Monero GUI, Feather and Cake.

- Balance and history are scanned on your computer, so your view key never leaves it. Kyro scans against a regular monerod node, over Tor.

- The first sync of an old restored wallet can take a while.

- Monero has no native staking.

- Same recovery phrase as your other 35 blockchains.

- Keys encrypted on your computer; every signature confirmed in a system window.

All wallet features How swap fees work How your keys are protected

At a glance

## Monero in one table

What works today, and through what.

What Kyro supports on Monero

|  | Available | Details

| Send and receive |  | XMR. Over Tor, with address-poisoning alerts.

| Swap from |  | Providers: Exolix. Kyro's fee is a second transfer.

| Swap to |  | The amount you see already has Kyro's fee out.

| Earn |  | Not offered.

| Ledger |  | Not supported.

| Trezor |  | Not supported.

Swap routes and limits How Kyro uses Tor

Questions

## Monero questions

Q: Is Kyro a free Monero wallet?
A: Yes. Kyro is free, open source and non-custodial. You pay the network fee when you send XMR, and your keys stay on your own computer.

Q: Can I swap XMR in Kyro?
A: Yes, in both directions. Providers: Exolix. Kyro's fee is a second transfer. Routes and limits.

Q: Can I earn on Monero in Kyro?
A: Kyro offers no staking or lending on Monero.

Q: Does Kyro work with a hardware wallet on Monero?
A: No. Monero is not supported on hardware wallets in Kyro. Use a software account.

Q: What can a server see when I use Monero in Kyro?
A: The node sees the blocks you download and the transactions you publish, from a Tor exit relay. It never gets your addresses or your view key, because Kyro scans blocks locally. Details.

Q: Can I use my existing recovery phrase for Monero?
A: Yes, if it is a standard 12 or 24-word BIP39 phrase. It covers all 36 blockchains. More questions.

# TON wallet for Windows, macOS and Linux

Yes

Kyro offers no staking or lending on TON.
No

### Hardware wallet

Sign TON transactions with a Ledger. The Ledger wallet has a different address than the software wallet. Comments: printable ASCII, up to 120 characters.
Yes

Details

## TON in Kyro

- TON is the network. Its coin is Gram (GRAM), renamed from Toncoin in June 2026.

- USDT on TON is supported.

- v4R2 wallet. The same recovery phrase gives the same address as Trust Wallet. Tonkeeper uses its own phrase format, so its addresses will not match.

- The wallet contract is deployed on your first send.

- Same recovery phrase as your other 35 blockchains.

- Keys encrypted on your computer; every signature confirmed in a system window.

A: The server sees the addresses and transactions you ask about, and the IP of a Tor exit relay, not yours. Zcash has its own circuit family, except that all EVM networks share one. Who sees what.

Q: Can I use my existing recovery phrase for Zcash?
A: Yes, if it is a standard 12 or 24-word BIP39 phrase. It covers all 36 blockchains. More questions.

================================================================
Tor wallet: built-in Tor for every request | Kyro Wallet
URL: https://kyrowallet.com/tor/
================================================================

Tor wallet

# Tor is built in, and it stays on

Balances, prices, swaps and broadcasts all leave through an embedded Tor client. You install nothing extra and set nothing up. If Tor is not ready, Kyro stops.

Download Kyro

The client

## One app, Tor included

Kyro embeds Arti, the Tor client from The Tor Project. It starts in the background when the app opens, and the wallet shows its state.

- The interface cannot reach any server. Only the Rust shell can, and only over the list below.

- Kyro contacts only the servers listed in docs/NETWORK.md, and refuses every other host.

- Only HTTPS is accepted, with one exception: the onion service for Bitcoin.

- Your custom servers go through Tor as well.

Circuits

## A circuit per blockchain

A server or an exit relay cannot link your Bitcoin lookup to your Solana lookup through the circuit, because they never share one.

### Isolated by family

Each blockchain family has its own isolated circuits. Prices and swaps have their own too. All EVM networks count as one family.

### Bitcoin stays inside Tor

Bitcoin lookups go to mempool's onion service. No exit relay is involved, so no relay sees the hostname or the volume.

### Retries stay on Tor

A stream refused by a closed circuit is retried on a new one. A refusal on one family no longer moves the others. It never falls back to clear.

Who sees what

## What each party sees

In Tor mode, the default. This table comes from the network document in the repo, which lists every server by name.

What each party sees when Kyro uses Tor

| Party | Sees | Does not see

| Your internet provider | That you use Tor | The hosts you reach, your addresses, your amounts

| First relay | Your IP address | The destination and the request

| Middle relay | Two other relays | You, and the request

| Exit relay | The hostname and the volume | You, and the content (TLS runs up to the server)

| Blockchain server | The addresses and transactions requested, from a Tor exit | Your IP address

| Monero node | Blocks downloaded and transactions you publish | Your IP, your addresses, your view key

| Price server (CoinGecko) | The coins and currency requested | Your IP address, your addresses

| Swap provider | Tokens, amounts and the recipient address | Your IP address

With Tor off, every server sees your IP address and your internet provider sees the hosts. Privacy policy

Fails closed

## No Tor, no request

If Tor is not ready within 60 seconds, the request fails with TOR_UNAVAILABLE. Nothing goes out in the clear, and there is no automatic fallback.

Leaving Tor is your decision. Kyro asks in a native system window drawn outside the interface, so a compromised page cannot turn Tor off without you.

Limits

## What Tor does not do

Tor is one layer. It hides your network location. These things stay true with it on.

### Servers still see lookups

The server you query sees the addresses and transactions you ask about. To avoid that, use your own node.

### Blockchains stay public

Most chains publish every transfer. Tor hides your IP, and your addresses remain linked to each other on chain when you link them.

### Swap providers see the order

Swap APIs see the tokens, amounts and recipient. Exolix sees your source and destination addresses, so it can link those two accounts.

### Two background requests

The signed update check and the anonymous weekly count. Both go over Tor and both can be turned off.

Questions

## Common questions

Q: Do I need to install Tor or Tor Browser?
A: No. Kyro embeds its own Tor client, Arti, from The Tor Project. It starts in the background when the app opens.

Q: Can I turn Tor off?
A: Yes. It is your choice in Settings, confirmed in a native system window, so a compromised interface cannot switch it off for you. In clear mode, servers see your IP address.

Q: Does Tor make my transactions anonymous?
A: No. Tor hides who is asking. It does not hide what is asked: the server you query still sees the addresses and transactions you look up, and public blockchains stay public.

Q: Why is Kyro slower over Tor?
A: Requests take three relays instead of a direct path, and some servers refuse some exit relays. Kyro retries on a new circuit, and each blockchain shows as soon as it answers.

Q: Do my own servers go through Tor too?
A: Yes. When Tor is on, your custom servers use the isolated circuits of their own blockchain family.

================================================================
Monero desktop wallet with Tor and local scanning | Kyro
URL: https://kyrowallet.com/monero/
================================================================

Monero desktop wallet · XMR

# Private Monero, on your desktop

Kyro keeps Monero honest: blocks are scanned on your own machine, your view key never leaves it, and every request goes over Tor.

Download Kyro XMR details

Local scanning

## The node sends blocks. Your machine reads them.

Light-wallet servers need your view key, so they see every incoming payment. Kyro uses none. It downloads blocks from a monerod node and the Rust core analyses them with a view key that stays on your computer.

- Default node: Cake Wallet's public node. You can replace it.

- The node never receives your addresses, spend key or view key.

- The scan state is stored on disk, encrypted.

- A lying node can hide incoming payments or delay your sync. It cannot steal funds.

Who sees what

## What the node learns

A Monero wallet has to talk to someone. Here is exactly what that costs you, with Tor on and off.

What a Monero node sees

|  | Tor on (default) | Tor off

| Block ranges you download | Yes, so your wallet's rough age | Yes

| Decoy outputs requested | Yes | Yes

| Transactions you publish | Yes | Yes

| Your IP address | No, a Tor exit relay. None on a .onion node | Yes, and it can be linked to what you publish

| Your addresses, view key, spend key, phrase | Never | Never

Keys

## One phrase, and an exit

Monero comes from the same recovery phrase as your other coins, with its own 25-word seed if you want to leave.

### Same recovery phrase

Your XMR derives from your BIP39 phrase, using the scheme of Ledger's Monero app. It is not a native 25-word Monero phrase.

### A way out

Kyro shows a 25-word Monero seed in the protected phrase window. It restores the wallet in Monero GUI, Feather or Cake Wallet.

### One limit

A 25-word phrase made elsewhere cannot be imported. Send those XMR to your Kyro address instead.

Swap

## In and out of XMR

Swap to or from Monero through Exolix: no account, no key, over Tor. BTC, LTC, DOGE, TRX, ETH, SOL, USDT and USDC all reach XMR, and XMR reaches them.

- Kyro checks that the order pays your own address and that the deposit address is valid.

- It then sends an ordinary transfer. No contract, no third-party transaction.

- Kyro's fee is a second ordinary transfer of the coin you sell. The swap value is reduced by the same rate as other swaps.

- Exolix sees your source and destination addresses and can link them.

Step by step: swap to Monero

Under the hood

## Rust, and no home-grown crypto

Monero is easy to get subtly wrong, so Kyro leans on a reviewed library and checks its own output.

### monero-oxide

Addresses, scanning, key images, CLSAG, Bulletproofs+ and decoy selection come from monero-oxide / monero-wallet 0.2. Cypher Stack audited that library in May 2025. Kyro itself has not been externally audited.

### Checked after signing

Rust builds the transfer, then verifies that the signed transaction creates exactly the outputs you approved.

### Honest status

This integration is young. There is no Monero on hardware wallets, and it is tested against official vectors. Start small.

Questions

## Common questions

Q: Is Kyro a full Monero wallet?
A: Yes. Send, receive and swap XMR from the same app as your other coins. Kyro talks to a monerod node and scans blocks itself. No light-wallet server is used.

Q: Does the Monero node see my addresses?
A: No. Neither your addresses nor your view key are sent. The node sees the block ranges you download, the decoy outputs requested for a send, and the transactions you publish, from a Tor exit relay.

Q: Can I import my 25-word Monero seed?
A: No. Kyro derives Monero from your BIP39 recovery phrase, and a 25-word phrase created elsewhere cannot be imported. The other way works: Kyro shows a 25-word seed that restores your wallet in Monero GUI, Feather or Cake Wallet.

Q: Can I use my own Monero node?
A: Yes. Set your own monerod in Settings, or a .onion address. Kyro checks it is on the right network and refuses to fall back to the default node if yours goes down.

Q: Does Monero work on a Ledger or Trezor in Kyro?
A: No. Monero on a hardware wallet is not supported.

Q: Why do I not see an old XMR payment?
A: Kyro scans from a starting block. If this phrase received XMR earlier, pick an older height in Settings > Security and it scans again from there.

Swap

# Any coin to any coin

Kyro asks several providers, shows what actually lands in your account and decodes the transaction before you sign. 33 blockchains, no account, over Tor.

Download Kyro Swap fees

How it works

## One screen, several providers

Pick what you hold, pick what you want. Kyro compares quotes and shows the amount you receive, with the fee already out.

Routes

## Where each coin can go

From the live coverage audit in the repo. Providers can change what they list, so a quote is the final word.

Swap routes by coin

| Coin or network | From | To | Providers

| Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base | Yes | Yes | 0x and LI.FI on the same chain. 1Click and LI.FI across chains. Exolix to XMR, KAS, ALGO and NEAR

| Polygon | Yes | Yes | 0x and LI.FI. 1Click. Exolix to XMR, KAS, ALGO and NEAR

| BNB Chain, Avalanche | Yes | Yes | 0x and LI.FI. 1Click

| Gnosis | Yes | Yes | LI.FI. 1Click

| Cronos, Mantle, Sonic, Flare, Kaia, HyperEVM, Sei | Yes | Yes | 0x or LI.FI, same chain only

Full coverage audit on GitHub

Fee

## Included in the rate, and public

The Kyro fee slides from 5% on a swap of $5 or less down to 0.7% from $10,000, and it is 0.9% when the token price is unknown. It funds the project.

- What you see as "You receive" already has the fee out.

- It is collected through each provider's official integrator mechanism.

- Exolix routes are the exception: the fee is a second ordinary transfer on the source chain.

- The rates live in one open file. Read fees.ts.

Fee table and calculator

Checks

## Swaps you can check

A swap is a transaction written by someone else. Kyro treats it that way.

### Decoded first

Kyro decodes the provider's transaction before asking for your password: recipient, minimum amount and fee.

### Official contracts

It checks that the transaction targets the provider's official contract.

### Exact approvals

Token approvals are for the exact amount. An unlimited approval needs an explicit action and shows a warning.

### Simulated

The transaction is simulated just before you sign it.

Limits

## What does not swap yet

Better here than in a failed quote.

- Stellar as a source. Stellar deposits need a memo, and Kyro only sends plain transfers to deposit addresses. You can swap into XLM.

- Polkadot. 1Click does not list it, and delivery to Asset Hub is not confirmed through Exolix.

- Cosmos Hub. 1Click does not list it, and Exolix refuses the pair.

- Conflux. No provider contract Kyro can check there.

- Tokens on NEAR and Algorand. Only the native coin is offered through Exolix. Other tokens on NEAR, Algorand, Polkadot, Stellar, TON, Sui and Aptos swap only if 1Click lists them.

- Cronos, Mantle, Sonic, Flare, Kaia, HyperEVM and Sei. Same chain only.

Questions

## Common questions

Q: Can I really swap any coin to any coin?
A: Almost. 33 of the 36 blockchains can swap, across chains in most cases. The table on this page lists the limits: Stellar is arrival only, some EVM networks swap on the same chain only, and Polkadot, Cosmos Hub and Conflux have no route yet.

Q: What does a swap cost?
A: A Kyro fee from 0.7% to 5% depending on the swap value, already taken out of the amount you see, plus the network fee. Full fee table.

Q: Do I need an account with a swap provider?
A: No. Kyro talks to the providers directly over Tor. There is nothing to sign up for.

Q: Why does a Monero swap send two transactions?
A: Exolix has no integrator fee, so Kyro's fee cannot be collected inside the swap. It goes as a second ordinary transfer of the sold coin. The same applies to any Exolix route.

Q: What if the rate changes before the swap lands?
A: You set a maximum slippage of 0.1%, 0.5%, 1% or your own value, and Kyro shows the guaranteed minimum before you sign.

Earn

# Earn, with the risks in plain sight

14 options in one list: staking, liquid staking and lending. No sign-up. Rates are estimates, never guaranteed.

Download Kyro

Demo numbers. Real rates are estimates, never guaranteed.

Options

## All 14 options

What you can put to work, how long it stays locked, and what works from a hardware wallet.

Earn options in Kyro

| Option | Type | Assets | Lock | Hardware wallet

| Ethereum · Lido | Liquid staking | ETH | stETH can be swapped. Unstaking goes through Lido's queue, often 1 to 5 days | Yes

| Aave · Ethereum | Lending | USDT, USDC, DAI, WETH | None | Yes

| Aave · Arbitrum | Lending | USDT, USDC | None | Yes

| Aave · Polygon | Lending | USDT, USDC | None | Yes

| Aave · Base | Lending | USDC | None | Yes

| Solana | Staking | SOL | About 2 to 3 days | No

| Cardano | Staking | ADA (2 ADA deposit, returned) | None | No

| TRON | Staking | TRX (minimum 1 TRX) | 14 days | No

| NEAR | Staking | NEAR | 4 epochs, about 2 to 3 days | No

Three kinds

## Three ways to earn

They look alike in a list. They are different underneath.

### Staking

SOL, ADA, TRX and NEAR. You delegate from your own account to a validator, pool or Super Representative. They cannot spend your coins. On Cardano your ADA stays spendable.

### Liquid staking

ETH with Lido. You receive stETH, and you can swap it or unstake through Lido's withdrawal queue, then claim in Kyro. You rely on Lido's contracts.

### Lending

Aave v3 on Ethereum, Arbitrum, Polygon and Base. You deposit tokens into a contract and earn the variable rate borrowers pay. You can withdraw when liquidity allows it.

Risks

## What can go wrong

Yields are variable and paid by the protocol. You can lose money. Read this before you start.

### Contract bugs

Lido and Aave are smart contracts Kyro does not control. A bug or an attack there can lose funds.

### Depeg

stETH can trade below ETH, and a stablecoin can lose its peg.

### Lower rewards

Rates move. A validator's commission, downtime or a retiring pool can cut your rewards. A delinquent Solana validator pays nothing until it returns.

### Waiting periods

TRON unstaking takes 14 days. Solana and NEAR take a few days, and Solana can take longer. You earn nothing in the meantime, and prices keep moving.

### Votes shrink

On TRON, unstaking reduces your votes in proportion. Kyro warns you first.

### Price risk

Staked coins can lose value like any other. A rate does not protect you from that.

Kyro is a tool. Nothing on this site is financial advice.

Signing

## See the contract, then sign

Every step shows the contract, the function and the exact amount. Approvals are for the exact amount only, never unlimited.

- Staking operations are a closed list. Everything else is refused, with your key as the only authority.

- On Solana, Kyro refuses authority changes and lockups.

- On NEAR, only pools from the official factories, with the expected code, are accepted.

- Risky choices, such as a commission above 10% on Solana, get a second confirmation.

- With a Ledger or Trezor, Kyro names the contract and function, then the device shows the transaction.

Step by step: stake SOL

Questions

## Common questions

Q: Are the rates guaranteed?
A: No. Every rate in Kyro is an estimate and it moves. For Solana, Cardano and TRON it is network-wide, before the validator, pool or Super Representative takes its share.

Q: Does Kyro take a fee on Earn?
A: Kyro takes no fee on staking. You pay the network fee, and validators, pools and protocols keep their own share of the rewards.

Q: Can I use Earn with a Ledger or Trezor?
A: Yes for Lido and Aave. Staking on Solana, Cardano, TRON and NEAR still needs a recovery-phrase account, and Kyro refuses it from a hardware account.

Q: Can a validator take my coins?
A: On Solana, Cardano, TRON and NEAR a validator, pool or Super Representative cannot spend your coins, and there is no slashing for delegators. A poor choice costs rewards.

Q: Is lending on Aave the same risk as staking?
A: No. Your tokens go into a smart contract. A contract bug or a stablecoin losing its peg can cost you money. Kyro cannot remove those risks.

Q: Is this financial advice?
A: No. Kyro shows options and their terms. Whether any of them suits you is your decision.

Windows desktop wallet

# Kyro for Windows

A private crypto wallet for 64-bit Windows. One command, or the installer. It installs for the current user and starts on its own.

Download Kyro

Install

## One command

It downloads the latest release from GitHub, checks its SHA-256 against SHA256SUMS and stops if they differ.

Windows · PowerShell

irm https://kyrowallet.com/install.ps1 | iex

macOS and Linux · Terminal

curl -fsSL https://kyrowallet.com/install.sh | sh

Downloads the latest release from GitHub, checks its SHA-256 against SHA256SUMS, then installs it. The scripts are open source: install.ps1 · install.sh (website/src).

Or the file

## Install by hand

- Run the one-line command in PowerShell, or download Kyro-windows-x64-setup.exe.

- If you used the file, verify its SHA-256 first.

- SmartScreen may show "Windows protected your PC". Click More info, then Run anyway.

- One Kyro window installs the app, starts it and closes. Kyro appears in the Start menu.

Kyro-windows-x64-setup.exeKyro-windows-x64.msiSHA256SUMS

Kyro-windows-x64-setup.exe: Recommended, updates itself. Kyro-windows-x64.msi: For managed installs, no self-update.

Notes

## Good to know on Windows

### SmartScreen

The installers are not code-signed yet, so a browser download triggers the warning. The one-line command and in-app updates do not. What SmartScreen means for Kyro.

### .exe or .msi

Prefer the .exe: it is the only Windows package that updates itself. The .msi does not.

### Updates

The installed app downloads signed updates over Tor, verifies them and applies them when you close it.

### Phrase window

The recovery phrase window is excluded from screenshots and screen sharing on Windows.

Same on every system

## The full wallet, everywhere

The Windows build is the same Kyro: 36 blockchains, swaps, Earn, hardware wallets and Tor from the first launch. The interface is in English and French.

- No account and no analytics.

- Your recovery phrase stays on your computer, encrypted.

- Your phrase also restores your wallet on another system.

About Kyro: why this private wallet exists | Kyro Wallet
URL: https://kyrowallet.com/about/
================================================================

About

# Why Kyro exists

A wallet sees more about you than almost any other app: what you own, what you spend and where you are. Kyro is built to see as little of that as it can.

## The problem

Holding your own keys protects your coins. It does nothing for your privacy on its own. Every balance check tells a server which addresses you care about and which IP address asked. Put enough of those requests in one log and your wallet has a name on it.

Most of that traffic is invisible, so nobody notices. Kyro starts from the other end: a desktop wallet where the private path is the default, and where you have to choose, in a system window, to leave it.

## What Kyro holds to

- Your keys are yours. The recovery phrase is encrypted on your computer. Nobody else, developers included, can move your funds.

- No account. No email, no sign-up, no server holding funds.

- No analytics. One anonymous weekly count over Tor, which you can turn off.

- You read what you sign. Rust decodes each transaction and a native window shows it.

- Limits are published. What Kyro cannot protect you from is written down, chain by chain.

## How it is paid for

Kyro is free. The swap fee, from 0.7%, funds the project, and it is public: the rates sit in one open source file. Sending, receiving and staking carry no Kyro fee. Donations and GitHub Sponsors help too.

## What Kyro is not

- It is not a bank, an exchange or a custodian. If you lose your phrase and your computer, nobody can recover your funds.

- It is not a promise of anonymity. Tor hides your IP address. Public blockchains stay public.

- It is not externally audited yet. An internal security review has been done; no independent audit has been published.

- It is not on your phone. Kyro is desktop only. A mobile app using the name is not ours.

## Keep reading

### Read the code

Licence, build instructions and how to contribute.

### See what is next

Roadmap

# Where Kyro is going

Version 1.0.6 today. This page lists what has shipped and what is planned. There are no dates, because a wallet ships when it is checked.

### Shipped

### 36 blockchains, one phrase

Bitcoin, EVM networks, Solana, TRON, Cardano, Monero and more, with 220+ tokens.

### Tor built in

On by default, a circuit per blockchain family, no fallback to a direct connection.

### Signed automatic updates

Downloaded over Tor, verified against a pinned public key, applied at the next start.

### Swaps across chains

Several providers compared, with Monero, Kaspa, Algorand and NEAR both ways through Exolix since 1.0.6.

### Earn

14 options since 1.0.5: Lido, Aave v3, and staking on Solana, Cardano, TRON and NEAR.

### Hardware wallets

Ledger and Trezor, one-step Ledger connect, SPL and TRC-20 token sends in 1.0.6.

### One-click Windows installer

A single branded window since 1.0.1, and one-line install on every system.

### Next, in no fixed order

### More staking

Polkadot, Sui and Aptos.

### Token sends on more chains

From hardware accounts, beyond EVM, Solana and TRON.

### Code signing

So Windows and macOS stop warning on first launch. See the code signing policy.

### winget

Install and update with the Windows package manager.

### More Ledger chains

Polkadot, Kaspa and Zcash on Ledger, where the device apps make it possible.

### Compact filters for Bitcoin

A private way to read Bitcoin without an address server, once its dependencies pass review.

### Reproducible builds

Bit-for-bit reproducible builds are a goal, not yet a guarantee.

Not today

## What Kyro will not rush

A few things cannot be done safely yet. They stay out until they can.

### Polkadot on Ledger

The Ledger app needs a metadata proof with each transaction, which Kyro does not build yet.

### Device authenticity

Kyro does not run Trezor's authenticity check. Do that in Trezor Suite.

### External audit

An internal review has been done. No independent audit has been published yet.

## More on the project

### Changelog

Every release, in plain words.

### Contribute

Issues and pull requests are welcome.

### About Kyro

Why it exists and how it is paid for.

Changelog

# What changed

Every release of Kyro, newest first. This page is generated from CHANGELOG.md at build time.

## 1.0.6Latest

- Switching between Portfolio and Assets no longer slides the tab underline across the screen.

- Ledger Litecoin: the app's protocol is detected by asking it (Litecoin 2.4.x is still the legacy app), and the account is read without the master key the app refuses, instead of being reported as outdated.

- Address book: the network is detected from the pasted address (a short choice only when several match), Enter saves and the name is optional. Send offers "Save" for a new recipient.

- History is fetched in the background after unlock and kept per wallet, so the History page opens on a ready list; while it refreshes, what is there shows with a small "Updating...". Unreachable networks are named in a calm line and retried on their own.

- Price charts: "All" now goes back years (Kraken public weekly prices, no account), and is hidden for coins without a long history instead of repeating 1Y.

- Arbitrum history works over Tor again: a second public node (arb1.arbitrum.io) is tried when publicnode refuses.

- Search: one result per coin, with its icon and your balance or its rank.

- Receive: a quieter network note.

- Swap: Monero, Kaspa, Algorand and NEAR can now be swapped FROM (Exolix), not only to.

- Ledger: Litecoin works with the current Litecoin app (keys, address on screen, signing over the new protocol); an app that does not understand Kyro now says to update it in Ledger Live.

- Hardware wallets: Solana tokens (SPL, e.g. USDC/USDT) can be sent from Ledger and Trezor accounts, creating the recipient's token account when needed; a Trezor shows the recipient wallet, a Ledger that needs it says "Enable Blind signing in the Solana app settings".

- Hardware wallets: TRON tokens (TRC-20, e.g. USDT) can be sent from Ledger accounts; when the Tron app needs a setting, Kyro names it ("Allow data" or "Custom contracts").

- Ledger: connect in one step, like Ledger Live. Every chain the Ledger supports is ticked; one "Connect" opens each app in turn, reads the keys, and skips an app that is not installed or refused. A short result per chain follows (Added / Not installed / Skipped).

## 1.0.5

- Earn (was Staking): a new page with 14 options and live estimated rates. New: ETH liquid staking with Lido (stake, unstake through the withdrawal queue, claim), and lending on Aave v3: USDT, USDC, DAI and WETH on Ethereum, USDT and USDC on Arbitrum and Polygon, USDC on Base. Every step shows the contract, the function and the exact amount; approvals are for the exact amount only.

- Activity: an asset page only waits for its own blockchain. Empty history is remembered, so "No activity" shows at once; a spinner never stays more than a few seconds.

- Charts fit the window in width and height.

- Earn opens from its last state, without grey placeholders.

- Notifications: one short style everywhere, starting with the update notice.

- Asset page: "Loading activity..." until the first answer, never "No activity" before it. The header wraps on narrow windows (the period selector stays whole).

- Earn: a rate that cannot be read shows "-" after a few seconds; the page scrolls normally.

- Token picker: Escape closes it.

- Swap: pick any coin you hold, on any network, without a network menu; the account choice only shows when you have several. The rate ("1 BTC ~ 31.2 ETH") and what you receive show under the amounts.

- Earn: live estimated rates for Solana, Cardano and TRON (network-wide, before the validator, pool or SR commission), read from the servers Kyro already uses.

- Earn with a Ledger or Trezor: Lido and Aave work from hardware wallet accounts. Kyro names the contract and function first, then the device shows the transaction; a Ledger with blind signing off gets a short hint. Staking on Solana, Cardano, TRON and NEAR still needs a recovery-phrase account.

## 1.0.4

- Staking: NEAR. Stake, unstake and withdraw with NEAR staking pools. Kyro only accepts pools from the official factories and checks the pool's code before each transaction.

- Swap: search by name or ticker in the coin picker. Monero shows in the list and can be bought from more coins (ETH on Arbitrum, Base, Optimism, POL, DOGE, TRX, USDT on TRON). Kaspa, Algorand and NEAR can now be received from a swap.

- Faster: charts are kept on your computer and only the recent part is refreshed. Each blockchain shows as soon as it answers. Staking opens from its last state.

- My assets: one row per crypto, with every account under it.

- Tokens from the top 250 (Quant and others) open as supported assets instead of "price only".

- Charts stay continuous at any window size. No more endless "Loading" on asset pages.

- Updates install when you close the window.

- Simpler texts in Settings, recovery phrase checks and update notices. Cleaner outgoing connections and API key screens.

## 1.0.3

- Swap: Monero. Swap BTC, LTC, ETH, SOL, USDT or USDC to XMR through Exolix (no account, no key, over Tor). Kyro creates the order, checks that it pays your own Monero address and that the deposit address is valid, then sends a normal transfer. Kyro's service fee is a second small transfer of the same coin. XMR to other coins comes later. Tested with live quotes only.

- Ledger: Kyro now opens the right app for you. Plug in and unlock the Ledger, click Connect, and approve "Open Bitcoin" (or Ethereum, Solana...) on the device when asked. If another app is open, Kyro closes it first. A missing app shows "Install the app with Ledger Live". Same when signing from a Ledger account. Not yet tested on a real Ledger.

## 1.0.2

- Tor: fixed history failing on EVM networks ("Protocol error while launching a data stream") and the slowness behind it. A server refusing one Tor exit no longer moves every network of the same family onto new circuits; requests per family are bounded; a stream refused by a just-closed circuit is retried on a new one. Tor still never falls back to clear.

- History: no more raw error text. A short message with Retry is shown instead; the technical detail is in Settings > Network diagnostics.

- History: activity shows at once from a local cache (amounts and transaction details only), then refreshes in the background; each blockchain appears as soon as it answers, without waiting for the slowest. No more long grey placeholder rows.

- Privacy: new anonymous weekly count (on by default, Settings > Privacy). Once a week, over Tor only, Kyro downloads a tiny file from its GitHub release so the download counter can estimate active wallets. No identifier and no personal data are sent.

## 1.0.1

- Windows: new one-click installer. No wizard any more: a single branded Kyro window installs the app for the current user, then starts Kyro and closes. Silent, passive and in-app update installs behave as before.

- Windows: the uninstaller now shows the Kyro icon instead of the default NSIS one.

## 1.0.0

- First stable release.

All releases and files on GitHub

Open source crypto wallet: read, build, verify | Kyro
URL: https://kyrowallet.com/open-source/
================================================================

Open source

# Don't trust it. Read it.

The interface, the Rust core and the app shell are all public under GPL-3.0-or-later. Here is how to read, build and verify what you run.

Source on GitHub

Read

## Where to start

A small map of the repository. Keys live in one place, and it has no network access.

Repository layout

| Path | What it holds

| crates/wallet-core | Pure Rust: vault, BIP39 and BIP32, derivation, decoding, signing. No network, no files

| apps/desktop/src-tauri | Tauri 2 shell: commands, session and auto-lock, filtered network access, native windows

| apps/desktop/src | React and strict TypeScript interface. No secrets

| packages/chains | Chain adapters that build unsigned transactions

| packages/swap | Swap providers and fee logic

| docs/ | Architecture, IPC contract, network requests, swap fees

Threat model Servers contacted Architecture Swap fees

Build

## Build it yourself

You need Rust 1.97.1, which rustup installs from the pinned toolchain file, Node.js 22+, pnpm 11 and the Tauri prerequisites for your system.

- Dependencies are pinned to exact versions, with committed lockfiles.

- CI runs cargo audit, cargo deny and pnpm audit.

- Before a PR: pnpm lint, pnpm typecheck, pnpm test.

Verify

## What you can check today

Three things you can verify, and one you cannot yet.

### Release checksums

Each release ships SHA256SUMS. Compare your file before you run it.

### Signed updates

Each update is signed. Kyro verifies it against a public key pinned in the app, and refuses a bad signature.

### Servers contacted

Every server is listed in NETWORK.md, and any new one has to be added there.

### Not yet

Bit-for-bit reproducible builds are a goal, not a guarantee. The installers are not code-signed yet.

Contribute

## Help make it better

Issues and pull requests are welcome.

- Run pnpm lint, pnpm typecheck and pnpm test before opening a pull request.

- Any new server Kyro contacts must be listed in docs/NETWORK.md.

- Changes to the IPC contract belong in docs/IPC.md.

- Never post a recovery phrase, private key or password in an issue, pull request or log.

## Report a vulnerability

Please do not open a public issue. Report privately through GitHub security advisories, with a proof of concept if you can. Reports are acknowledged within 72 hours, with a fix and coordinated disclosure within 90 days at most.

Questions

## Common questions

Q: What licence is Kyro under?
A: GPL-3.0-or-later. You can read, run, change and share it. If you distribute a changed version, it stays under the same licence, with its source.

Q: Are Kyro builds reproducible?
A: Not bit for bit yet. It is a goal, not a guarantee. Today you can verify the SHA-256 of a release and build from the same source yourself.

Q: Can I remove the swap fee?
A: Yes, in your own build. The rates live in packages/swap/src/fees.ts, and anyone can change them or set the fee to 0.

Q: Has Kyro been audited?
A: An internal security review has been done. No independent external audit has been published yet. Like all GPL software, Kyro comes with no warranty.

## Name and description

Write Kyro or Kyro Wallet. Short description:

Kyro Wallet is a free, open-source, non-custodial desktop wallet for Windows, macOS and Linux. One recovery phrase for 36 blockchains, keys on your own computer, Tor on by default.

## Type

Headlines use Archivo. Everything else uses Geist. Both are under the SIL Open Font License, with the licence files in OFL-Geist and OFL-Archivo.

## Usage

- Use the files as they are, with room around them.

- Use the dark version on dark backgrounds and the light version on light ones.

- Link to kyrowallet.com, the only official site, and to GitHub Releases for downloads.

- Do not change the colours or shape of the mark.

- Do not suggest that Kyro endorses your product or service.

- Do not use the name or logo for an app, a token or a download of your own.

## Facts to check

Kyro has no mobile app and no external audit published yet. The current version is 1.0.6. If you are unsure of a claim, the site summary and the repository are the reference.

First steps with Kyro: set up your wallet | Kyro Wallet

================================================================

Guide

# First steps with Kyro

Ten calm minutes: install, choose how to start, save your phrase, then try a small amount before you move anything serious.

2 min read

## 1. Install Kyro

The quickest way is the one-line command. It downloads the latest release from GitHub and checks its SHA-256 before installing.

Windows · PowerShell

irm https://kyrowallet.com/install.ps1 | iex

macOS and Linux · Terminal

curl -fsSL https://kyrowallet.com/install.sh | sh

Downloads the latest release from GitHub, checks its SHA-256 against SHA256SUMS, then installs it. The scripts are open source: install.ps1 · install.sh (website/src).

If you prefer the file, download it and verify it first.

## 2. Choose how to start

The welcome screen offers three ways in. There is no account in any of them.

- Use a Ledger or Trezor. Your keys stay in the device, and Kyro stores only public keys.

- Create a new vault. Kyro makes a new recovery phrase, 24 words by default.

- Import a recovery phrase. 12 or 24 BIP39 words from another wallet.

## 3. Pick a password

At least 10 characters, and a phrase of four words or more is better. It encrypts the vault on this computer, and you will type it to unlock Kyro and to sign. It cannot be recovered.

## 4. Write down your phrase

Kyro shows the words in a separate window, blurred until you choose to show them. Write them on paper, in order, then type the three words Kyro asks for. How to keep that paper safe.

## 5. Look around

Portfolio shows your total and your assets. Swap, Earn and History sit in the side rail. Ctrl K searches assets and addresses. The vault panel shows Tor, auto-lock and whether any unlimited approval is active.

Tor needs a moment to connect at launch. If it is not ready within 60 seconds, a request fails and nothing is sent in the clear.

## 6. Receive, then send a little

- Open an asset and choose Receive. Copy the address, or use the QR code.

- Send a small amount from wherever your coins are now.

- Back in Kyro, check that it arrives.

- Send a small amount out. Kyro asks for your password, then shows the decoded transaction in a system window. Read it, then confirm.

## Worth a look in Settings

- Privacy. The anonymous weekly count is on by default, over Tor only. You can turn it off here.

- Security. Check your phrase again, and for Monero, set the scan height.

- Networks. Point a blockchain at your own node.

How to verify your Kyro download with SHA-256 | Kyro Wallet
URL: https://kyrowallet.com/guides/verify-your-download/
================================================================

Guide

# Verify your download

A wallet is a bad thing to install from a fake link. This takes two minutes and proves your file matches the published release.

2 min read

## Where Kyro comes from

Kyro is published only on GitHub Releases. The links on our download page point there. There is no mobile app, so anything in an app store using the name is not ours.

## The easy way

The one-line install does this check for you. It compares the SHA-256 of the file with SHA256SUMS, and stops if they differ. Read the scripts first if you like: install.ps1 and install.sh.

## By hand

- Download your installer and SHA256SUMS into the same folder.

- Run the command for your system.

- Compare the result with the line for your file in SHA256SUMS. Every character must match.

## If the hashes differ

Delete the file and download it again from GitHub Releases. Do not run it.

## What this proves, and what it does not

A match proves your file is the one listed in that release, with no corruption and no swap along the way. It does not prove the code is free of bugs, and it depends on the release itself being genuine.

Two more honest limits. The installers are not code-signed yet, so your system warns on first launch: check the hash before you click through. Bit-for-bit reproducible builds are a goal, not a guarantee yet. If you want more certainty, build Kyro from source.

## After the first install

Updates verify themselves. Each one is signed, and Kyro checks the signature against a public key built into the app before installing. A bad signature is rejected.
